public_input.protocol_text: A purified enzyme converts substrate into a fluorescent product. Vehicle and no-enzyme controls, fixed substrate concentration and initial-rate conditions are specified. Compound A at 10 micromolar lowers the primary fluorescent signal by 70 percent in three independent preparations. A product-spike counterassay measures readout interference, and a separately validated LC-MS assay directly measures the same product with matrix-matched internal standards. The two assays use matching reaction conditions. The product-spike signal falls by 70 percent and LC-MS shows unchanged product formation across three preparations. The claim is biochemical inhibition in this assay; no cellular or therapeutic conclusion is drawn.
public_input.stated_objective: Determine whether compound A reduces enzyme-catalyzed product formation by approximately 70 percent at the stated concentration.

public_input.protocol_text: Probe P absorbs only within 480–500 nm under the stated buffer conditions; absorption outside this interval is negligible for this measurement. public_input.protocol_text: Probe U is characterized in the same solvent, temperature and concentration as the assay. Independent characterization shows that lowering pH from 7.40 to 6.00 produces a fivefold intensity increase without T. Between pH 7.38 and 7.42 the response varies by at most 3 percent. Analyte-only blanks, equal optical density, matched illumination and a linear detector exclude the stated optical alternatives. The supplied assay signal increases fivefold after T addition. Final pH is 7.40 in probe-only and 6.00 in target-containing samples, measured after addition. The intended conclusion is a target-associated response under pH-controlled conditions, without assigning a chemical reaction mechanism.
public_input.stated_objective: Attribute a fivefold fluorescence increase to addition of target T rather than a pH change.

The assigned concentration will be used as the dose coordinate; biological activity itself is not inferred from this preparation.

public_input.protocol_text: A purified enzyme converts substrate into a fluorescent product. Vehicle and no-enzyme controls, fixed substrate concentration and initial-rate conditions are specified. Compound A at 10 micromolar lowers the primary fluorescent signal by 70 percent in three independent preparations. A product-spike counterassay measures readout interference, and a separately validated LC-MS assay directly measures the same product with matrix-matched internal standards. The two assays use matching reaction conditions. The product-spike signal changes by 2 percent and LC-MS shows 68 percent less product in a single preparation. The claim is biochemical inhibition in this assay; no cellular or therapeutic conclusion is drawn.
public_input.stated_objective: Determine whether compound A reduces enzyme-catalyzed product formation by approximately 70 percent at the stated concentration.

public_input.protocol_text: A reversible inhibitor is tested against a purified enzyme under stable initial-rate conditions with constant solvent. Vehicle defines zero inhibition and a validated full-inhibition control defines 100 percent. Readout interference is excluded in a counterassay. Three independently prepared series have similar responses. The response is assumed monotonic over the tested range. A four-parameter logistic model with free plateaus is specified, and numerical uncertainty is to be reported. Ten concentrations from 0.001 to 30 micromolar span 2–98 percent inhibition, with several points around 50 percent and a fitted IC50 of 0.30 micromolar. The claimed potency applies only to these assay conditions.
public_input.stated_objective: Estimate an approximate IC50 for compound B from the supplied normalized concentration–response series.
